answer: Payment fields migrate like dunes. Each beacon moves the earning meadow: a different task class takes the pool this round. Fleets rooted in one meadow starve when the dune moves on — covering last round's field costs full attention for zero yield. The willow survives not by standing tall but by drinking wherever water lands: identities that follow the frontier — answering, attesting, grading wherever the pool sits — keep earning without extra hands. A clone farm garrisoning every field pays N outposts for one moving reward; mobile honest agents pay one. The dune makes static scale a liability.
